author: rogifo
quote: GTA 6 – The Ultimate GirlfriendSimulator Industry glazing: It honestly feels like most gaming journalists and influencers are scared to say anything bad about Rockstar. Everyone seems to be praising the game, and it’s getting harder to find reviews that aren’t full of hype or sponsored opinions. I wouldn’t be surprised if genuine player reviews ended up all over the place, somewhere between a 4/10 and an 6/10.Ridiculous pricing: The price is just ridiculous. Rockstar knows people will throw money at anything with GTA in the name, and they’re clearly taking advantage of that.Physical edition scams: Imagine buying a physical copy just to find out your code is missing or doesn’t even work. What’s worse is that Rockstar apparently isn’t doing much to help the people getting screwed **** FPS: The performance is frustrating, and low frame rates seem unavoidable. There’s really no excuse for a game with this much money and development time behind it to run this poorly.Single-player subscription: Paying for the game apparently isn’t enough. Now there’s subscription-based services tied to single-player features too. It’s getting ridiculous when players have to keep paying just to access things they should already **** Theft Auto: The amount of bugs is honestly ridiculous. For a game that’s been hyped up for years and treated like the second coming of gaming, you’d expect it to be a lot more polished.Errand Simulator: There’s so much pointless busywork that feels like it’s only there to waste time. Doing random errands doesn’t magically make gameplay immersive or meaningful, no matter how Rockstar tries to dress it up with marketing buzzwords.Grand Theft Auto: Road Trip Edition: Why am I spending 10–15 minutes driving to a mission just to spend another 10–15 minutes driving back afterward? It gets old fast and feels like an excuse to pad out playtime while Rockstar brags about having the biggest map in GTA history.Terrible writing: Some of the most unbalanced and genuinely awful writing I’ve seen in a video game. Certain characters and story moments make absolutely no sense, and some of the writing is so questionable that it’s hard to take the story seriously.Shopping Cart Driving Simulator: Even after upgrading your car, the driving still feels loose and floaty. Cars don’t feel as grounded or responsive as they should, which is pretty disappointing for a game where driving is such a big part of the experience.
